goal: Lackluster Plus+ is a running TV-channels web app: a small Node gateway (dist/, Fastify, plain JavaScript ES modules) that signs viewers in with their Plex account and serves one page (public/index.html) with the guide and the player. Today signing in opens a popup window, which TV browsers cannot handle. This plan changes ONLY the sign-in: a 4-character code typed at plex.tv/link on a phone (for TVs), and a same-tab sign-in (for computers). Everything else in the app stays exactly as it is.
rules: Only the sign-in changes. The guide, the player, chat, casting, the admin pages and every other route and function stay exactly as they are.
Sign-in never opens a window or a tab: no window.open, no target="_blank" for it.
The pin a browser is signing in with is known to the server ONLY from the signed lp_pin cookie; a pin id from the query string or the body is never used.
No secrets in the code or the tests: no tokens, no .env file, no real server addresses. Tests talk to the stand-in in tests/_t.py, never to the real plex.tv.
Names, ids, routes, JSON keys and exact strings are the ones in the brief and the tests.
The brand stays: the page says Lackluster Plus+ and Philibert TV by Esteef.Ai, as it does now.
conventions: JavaScript as the file already writes it: dist/ uses 4-space indents and single quotes; public/index.html uses 2-space indents and single quotes in its script.
Run a task's test with: .venv\Scripts\python.exe tests\<file>.py (it prints PASS/FAIL lines and starts the server itself).
Scratch files and experiments go in the system temp folder, never in the project folder.

tasks.title: Sign-in routes: a short code, a same-tab sign-in, a pin nobody else can poll
tasks.brief:
The sign-in routes of the gateway get two new ways to sign in that need no popup window, and a security hole is closed. Three files, in this order. They are plain JavaScript; after each edit run `node --check <file>`.

1. dist/config.js - in the `config` object, right after the line `plexProduct: 'Lackluster Plus+',` add two entries:
   plexTvUrl: (process.env.PLEX_TV_URL ?? 'https://plex.tv').replace(/\/+$/, ''),
   plexAuthAppUrl: process.env.PLEX_AUTH_APP_URL ?? 'https://app.plex.tv/auth/',
   (The tests set both to a local stand-in, so no test talks to the real Plex.)

2. dist/plexClient.js
   a. Delete the line `const PLEX_TV = 'https://plex.tv';` and use `config.plexTvUrl` everywhere PLEX_TV was used. After this the file must not contain the text https://plex.tv or https://app.plex.tv anywhere, comments included.
   b. createPin becomes `export async function createPin(opts = {})`:
      - `const strong = opts.strong !== false;` POST to `${config.plexTvUrl}/api/v2/pins` and add `?strong=true` ONLY when strong. (Without it Plex gives a short 4-character code a person can type at plex.tv/link.)
      - authUrl is built as now, but starts with `${config.plexAuthAppUrl}#!?clientID=` (the config value already ends with a slash). When opts.forwardUrl is set, append `&forwardUrl=` + encodeURIComponent(opts.forwardUrl) at the very END of authUrl.
      - still returns { pin, authUrl }.
   c. pollPin(pinId) now returns an object, never a bare token: if the response status is 404 return { status: 'expired' }; if it is otherwise not ok, throw as now; if the body has an authToken return { status: 'ok', authToken: body.authToken }; else { status: 'pending' }.
   Leave getPlexUser (apart from the URL), checkServerAccess and listSectionGenres as they are.

3. dist/auth/routes.js
   a. Above registerAuthRoutes add: `const PIN_COOKIE = 'lp_pin';` and three small helpers:
      - rememberPin(reply, pinId): reply.setCookie(PIN_COOKIE, String(pinId), { httpOnly: true, sameSite: 'lax', secure: process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production', path: '/', maxAge: 1800, signed: true });
      - forgetPin(reply): reply.clearCookie(PIN_COOKIE, { path: '/' });
      - readPin(req): `const raw = req.cookies[PIN_COOKIE]; if (!raw) return null; const got = req.unsignCookie(raw); const id = got.valid ? Number(got.value) : 0; return id > 0 ? id : null;`
      Why: Plex's pin ids are plain numbers that count up. Today /auth/plex/poll takes the pin id from the query string, so anyone can poll the numbers next to their own and be handed another person's session. From now on the pin is known ONLY from this signed cookie.
   b. POST /auth/plex/start - the handler takes (req, reply) and looks at `req.body?.mode`:
      - 'link': `const { pin } = await createPin({ strong: false });` rememberPin; send { mode: 'link', code: pin.code, linkUrl: 'https://plex.tv/link', qrUrl: pin.qr ?? null, expiresIn: pin.expiresIn ?? 900 }.
      - 'redirect': `const forwardUrl = `${req.protocol}://${req.host}/?signin=return`;` then createPin({ forwardUrl }); rememberPin; send { mode: 'redirect', authUrl }.
      - anything else, including no body at all (a page cached before this change): createPin(); rememberPin; send { pinId: pin.id, code: pin.code, authUrl } exactly as today.
      The pin id is in the answer ONLY in that last case.
   c. GET /auth/plex/poll - ignore req.query.pinId completely. `const pinId = readPin(req);` if there is none: status 400 with { status: 'none', error: 'No sign-in is in progress in this browser.' }. Then `const pin = await pollPin(pinId);`. If pin.status is 'pending': send { status: 'pending' }. Otherwise call forgetPin(reply) first; if 'expired': send { status: 'expired' } (status 200). Otherwise continue with `const authToken = pin.authToken;` and the code that is there now (getPlexUser, hasServerAccess, the 403 'denied' answer, createSession, the 'ok' answer), unchanged.
   Leave /auth/me and both /auth/logout routes as they are.

Run the test: .venv\Scripts\python.exe tests\test_signin_api.py - it starts the gateway itself. Every check must pass.
